_why: #1287 (Gate 5 of epic #1320). Every CI alert path in this repo was unfired, and three marker
labels did not exist — `ci-conservation-alert`, `ci-reasons-alert`, `ci-owasp-watch-alert`.
Each alert step carries a self-healing `gh label create`, so a MISSING MARKER LABEL IS PROOF
the path never executed. An alert path that has never fired is indistinguishable from one that
cannot fire, so this file records the run that PROVED each one, and src/cli/validate-alert-paths.ts
refuses a path with no proof. Re-prove any of them with:
gh workflow run <workflow name> -f alert_drill=true
which opens, comments on and then closes a self-cleaning `… — alert-path drill` issue under the
real job token.
#1348 (2026-07-28) unified the drill onto the production find-or-update branch (previously a
hand-written parallel branch sharing only the label-create step and the raw gh primitives — see
the action's own header). The five proof runs below were re-taken against that fix, on one
branch back to back, and a negative control (breaking find_or_update's `gh issue comment` call)
was run live and confirmed red (run 30331463282, jharvieux/Harvey#1391) before being reverted.
#1288 (2026-07-28) added `pendingProof` — the one disclosed way a path may sit here unproven.
It is built to fail loud, not open: `tracking` must name an OPEN issue (re-read by --labels),
the marker label is excluded from expectedLabels while pending BECAUSE its absence is the
evidence, and pendingProof and provenBy are mutually exclusive.
#1333 (2026-07-31) NARROWED the reason above, which was too broad and had gone stale into a
standing excuse. It read: `a drill can only be dispatched against a workflow that is ALREADY on
the default branch, so a brand-new alerting workflow cannot be proven before it merges`. Only
the first clause survives measurement. What GitHub actually requires is that the workflow FILE
exist on the default branch (#1288's TRIED evidence is a 404 on a file that did not: `HTTP 404:
workflow secbench.yml not found on the default branch`). It does NOT require the INPUTS, JOBS or
STEPS to be there — a workflow_dispatch run executes the copy on the `--ref` you name, so a
newly-declared `alert_drill` input is dispatchable from the branch that declares it. MEASURED
2026-07-31, four times on an unmerged branch, each dispatch accepted and each run executing the
422 recorded in alert-paths.yml's header (`Unexpected inputs provided: ["alert_drill"]`) did
not reproduce. Consequence: a NEW alert path in an EXISTING workflow file needs no hatch at all
— drill it on the branch before you ask for review. The hatch remains for the genuine case, a
workflow file that does not yet exist on main.
The same measurement discharged two hatches that had simply outlived their reason: free-recall
and semantic-freshness had both long since merged, so `cannot be proven before it merges` was
true when written and false when read. Both drilled 2026-07-31 and recorded below.
#1612 (2026-07-31) retired the last hatch that was NOT about a missing file, and the way it
failed is worth more than the fix. Its `why` read 'NOT ATTEMPTED this round' — and the attempt
had ALREADY BEEN MADE, by the run recorded two entries above as ci-heavy-cli-alert's own proof.
Run 30607143343 is a `-f alert_drill=true` dispatch on main; its job list ends `a red main raises
an alarm  success`, and it opened, commented on and closed drill issue #1642 under the
ci-main-red-alert marker at 05:37Z. This file's own workflow comment says so in advance ('ONE
dispatch proves both of this workflow's alert paths, each into its own marker namespace') — the
second half was simply never recorded. So the hatch was born stale: the marker label existed, and
'its absence is the evidence the path never ran' was false the moment it was written. #1650, a
REAL non-drill alarm from run 30609450580 at 06:25Z, then fired the production branch too.
A hatch is a claim like any other, and one written in the same hour as its own refutation is the
reason `--labels` re-reads the tracking issue instead of trusting the text.
Re-drilled anyway, at a known sha and under the current find-or-update.sh, because that is what
provenBy records: run 30664857256, drill issue #1729, `PROVED ci-main-red-alert`. The hatch's
other claim — a COST, 'proving it means a full red ci.yml run' during a live merge train — was
an estimate nobody had priced, and is now MEASURED and small: dispatched 20:57:55Z, main-red's
step reported PROVED at 21:01:50Z. Under four minutes, because `alert_drill` fails heavy-cli
shard 1 on its FIRST step, before install, so the only wait is shards 2 and 3 finishing normally.
A dispatch run also reports on no PR's head sha, so nothing in the merge train was gated on it.

unconverted.why: The news path, not a failure path: it fires when upstream MOVES, so it has no failure branch to drill. It is also the one alerting path that has demonstrably run — it opened issue #1218 under the real job token on a manual dispatch, 2026-07-27. Its find-or-update is inlined rather than using the shared action because it stamps the last-reported state into the issue body for idempotence, which the shared action does not model.

_scheduledWithoutAlertPath: Empty since #1333 (2026-07-31), and that is the point of leaving the key here rather than
deleting it: this is the ONE hatch in this gate that fails OPEN. A scheduled workflow listed
here goes red on a branch nobody watches and raises nothing; only the tracking issue carries it,
which is why checkDisclosureTracking re-reads that issue and fails when it is closed. The four
workflows that sat here — alert-paths, dry-run-drift, osv-staleness, corpus-m8 — now alert and
are recorded above with their drill runs.
